key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer formed by ion exchange during co-evaporation can passivate the rear contact of pure CuInSe2 bottom cells and enable >16% efficiency with a 552 mV VOC.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical rear-contact engineering route for low-bandgap chalcopyrite bottom cells suited to tandem photovoltaics without relying on Ag or heavy-alkali additions.
method: Formed GaOx in situ during co-evaporation of the CuInSe2 absorber via ion exchange.
Tested whether extra Cu, Na, or sputtering oxygen flow were required for GaOx conductivity.
Evaluated device performance after optimizing the passivating hole transport layer.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for the optimized CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: The conductive behavior appears sensitive to formation conditions and partial crystallinity, so transferability to other back-contact stacks may be limited.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
